newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines raises bank liquidity reserve.
newsitem.headline: Philippines raises bank liquidity reserve.

text.p: The Philippine Monetary Board has raised banks' liquidity reserves to three percent from two percent to mop up excess liquidity in the system, governor Gabriel Singson said on Monday.
The liquidity reserves are the portion of the reserve requirement that should be placed in the form of short-term, market-yielding government securities issued by the central bank.
The central bank said in a statement the increase in liquidity reserves will apply not only to deposits but also to common trust funds.
The increase in reserve requirements against such funds is expected to contract liquidity by 10.6 billion pesos, the statement said.

Despite the high interest rates, there was excess liquidity in the system caused by the lower volume of weekly Treasury bill offerings, outflows from the stock market and funds that were not reinvested in central bank bills, central bank managing director Amando Tetangco told reporters.
The central bank also said its move to cut the overnight borrowing rate further to 22 percent from 25 percent was aimed at encouraging banks to further lower their lending rates.
"The move has been made possible with the continued improvement in the foreign exchange market," Singson said.
The central bank also said it wanted to normalise credit growth which had slowed to 29.6 percent in May 1997 from a 54.5 percent high in September 1996.
The peso fell prey to the currency turmoil in the region for months, which eventually led to its de facto devaluation two weeks ago.
